questions.prompt: Is it difficult for you to concentrate in a noisy place?
questions.sampleA1:
Yes. Noise... difficult. I no like noise.

I like quiet.
questions.sampleA2:
Yes, it's difficult. I don't like noise because I can't think.

I like quiet places, and I study there.

Noise is bad for study.
questions.sampleB1:
Yes, it is difficult for me to concentrate when it's noisy.

I think I need a quiet place to work well.

For example, if people are talking loudly, I can't focus.

So, I usually go to the library.
questions.sampleB2: To be honest, yes, I really struggle to concentrate when there's a lot of noise around me. I get distracted at the drop of a hat, especially by people chatting nearby. So I usually put on my headphones and try to block out the background noise. That said, a bit of soft music actually helps me focus.
questions.uzSampleA1:
Ha. Shovqin... qiyin. Menga shovqin yoqmaydi.

Menga tinchlik yoqadi.
questions.uzSampleA2:
Ha, qiyin. Men shovqinni yoqtirmayman, chunki o'ylay olmayman.

Men tinch joylarni yaxshi ko'raman va u yerda o'qiyman.

Shovqin o'qish uchun yomon.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, shovqin bo'lganda diqqatimni jamlash men uchun qiyin.

O'ylashimcha, yaxshi ishlash uchun menga tinch joy kerak.

Masalan, agar odamlar baland ovozda gaplashsa, men diqqatimni jamlay olmayman.

Shuning uchun, men odatda kutubxonaga boraman.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Umuman olganda, ha, shovqinli joyda diqqatimni jamlash men uchun ancha qiyin.

Men osonlikcha tovushlardan, ayniqsa suhbatlar yoki to'satdan chiqqan baland shovqinlardan chalg'iyman.

Bu murakkab vazifalarga e'tibor qaratish qobiliyatimga juda ta'sir qiladi.

Shuning uchun, men chalg'ituvchi omillarni kamaytirish va diqqatimni yaxshilash uchun tinch joylarni qidirishga yoki shovqinni bekor qiluvchi naushniklardan foydalanishga harakat qilaman.

Biroq, ba'zida ozgina fon shovqini menga unchalik xalaqit bermaydi, bu shovqinning turiga bog'liq.

vocabulary.title: Q1 - Is it difficult for you to concentrate in a noisy place?
idioms: Silence is golden - "Sukunat - oltin"
in one ear and out the other - "bir quloqdan kirib, ikkinchisidan chiqmoq"
keep your eye on the ball - "e'tiboringizni asosiy narsaga qaratmoq"
sentenceStarters: "Yes, I find it quite difficult to concentrate when..." - "Ha, men ... bo'lganda diqqatimni jamlash juda qiyin"
"Usually, when I need to study..." - "Odatda, men o'qishim kerak bo'lganda..."
"However, I've noticed that some people can..." - "Biroq, ba'zi odamlar ... ekanligini payqadim"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Yes, I find it quite difficult to concentrate when there's a lot of noise around me. I'm the type of person who needs a peaceful environment to focus properly.
Usually, when I need to study or work on something important, I prefer to find a quiet spot, like a library or my own room. Background noise, especially loud conversations or music, can be incredibly distracting for me.
However, I've noticed that some people can block out distractions much more easily. Personally, I sometimes use noise-cancelling headphones to help me stay focused. As they say, "Silence is golden".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Ha, atrofimda shovqin ko'p bo'lganda diqqatimni jamlash men uchun ancha qiyin. Men tinch muhit kerak bo'lgan odamman, shunda yaxshi diqqatni jamlay olaman.

Odatda, o'qishim yoki muhim bir ish ustida ishlashim kerak bo'lsa, kutubxona yoki o'z xonam kabi tinch joy topishni afzal ko'raman. Orqa fondagi shovqin, ayniqsa baland suhbatlar yoki musiqa, men uchun juda chalg'ituvchi bo'lishi mumkin.

Biroq, ba'zi odamlar chalg'ituvchi omillarni ancha oson bartaraf eta olishini payqadim. Shaxsan men, ba'zan diqqatimni jamlashga yordam berish uchun shovqinni bekor qiluvchi naushniklardan foydalanaman. Aytishlaricha, "Tinchlik - oltin".

questions.prompt: How often do you buy new shoes?
questions.sampleA1: I buy shoes. Not often. Maybe one time a year. Shoes are good.
questions.sampleA2: I buy shoes sometimes. I like shoes, but they are expensive. I buy them when my old shoes are broken. And I buy shoes if I see nice shoes in the shop.
questions.sampleB1: I don't buy new shoes very often. I think maybe two or three times a year. It depends, because if my shoes are still good, I don't need new ones. However, if I see a pair I really like, I might buy them, even if I don't need them. Also, I need different shoes for different activities.
questions.sampleB2: Honestly, I don't buy new shoes all that often — maybe two or three times a year at most. The thing is, I tend to wear mine until they're completely worn out rather than chasing the latest trends. That said, if I come across a really comfortable pair, I'll happily splash out on them.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men oyoq kiyim sotib olaman. Tez-tez emas. Balki yiliga bir marta. Oyoq kiyimlar yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men ba'zan poyabzal sotib olaman. Poyabzal menga yoqadi, lekin ular qimmat turadi. Men ularni eski poyabzallarim yaroqsiz bo'lib qolganda sotib olaman. Va agar do'konda chiroyli poyabzal ko'rsam, poyabzal sotib olaman.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Men yangi poyabzallarni unchalik tez-tez sotib olmayman. O'ylashimcha, yiliga ikki yoki uch marta. Bu bog'liq, chunki agar poyabzallarim hali ham yaxshi bo'lsa, menga yangilari kerak emas.
Shunga qaramay, agar menga juda yoqqan bir juft poyabzalni ko'rsam, ularga ehtiyojim bo'lmasa ham, sotib olishim mumkin. Bundan tashqari, menga turli xil mashg'ulotlar uchun har xil poyabzallar kerak.
questions.uzSampleB2: Men yangi poyabzallarni yiliga bir necha marta, ehtimol ko'pi bilan ikki yoki uch marta sotib olaman. Bu, asosan, hozirgi poyabzallarim qancha vaqtga yetishiga va ko'zimga ayniqsa tushadigan narsa bormi yoki yo'qligiga bog'liq. Men moda ortidan quvishdan ko'ra qulaylik va chidamlilikka ustunlik beraman, shuning uchun poyabzallar modadan qolgani uchun emas, balki eskirganida almashtirishga ko'proq moyilman. Biroq, agar men chindan ham noyob yoki yaxshi ishlangan poyabzalga duch kelsam, istisno qilishga vasvasaga tushishim mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Q2 - How often do you buy new shoes?
idioms: A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step - "Ming millik sayohat bitta qadamdan boshlanadi"
walk a mile in someone's shoes - "birovning o'rnida bo'lmoq"
if the shoe fits, wear it - "agar poyabzal to'g'ri kelsa, kiy"
sentenceStarters: "To be honest, I don't buy new shoes very..." - "Rostini aytsam, men yangi poyabzal ... sotib olmayman"
"I'm not really someone who follows..." - "Men ... ga ergashuvchi odam emasman"
"However, I do believe in investing in..." - "Biroq, men ... ga sarmoya kiritishga ishonaman"

questions.sampleAnswer:
To be honest, I don't buy new shoes very frequently. I'd say I purchase a new pair roughly once or twice a year.
I'm not really someone who follows fashion trends closely, so I tend to buy shoes only when my old ones are worn out or when I need something specific, like formal shoes for an event or new trainers for exercise.
However, I do believe in investing in good quality footwear because comfortable shoes make a huge difference in daily life. As they say, "A journey of a thousand miles begins with a single step" — and it's better if that step is in comfortable shoes!
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Rostini aytsam, men yangi poyabzallarni unchalik tez-tez sotib olmayman. Men yiliga taxminan bir yoki ikki marta yangi poyabzal sotib olaman, deb ayta olaman.

Men moda tendentsiyalariga unchalik yaqindan ergashadigan odam emasman, shuning uchun men poyabzallarni faqat eski poyabzallarim eskirganda yoki biron bir aniq narsa kerak bo'lganda, masalan, tadbir uchun rasmiy poyabzal yoki mashq qilish uchun yangi krossovkalar kerak bo'lganda sotib olaman.

Biroq, men sifatli poyabzalga sarmoya kiritishga ishonaman, chunki qulay poyabzallar kundalik hayotda katta farq qiladi. Aytishlaricha, "Ming milyalik sayohat birinchi qadamdan boshlanadi" - va bu qadam qulay poyabzalda bo'lsa, yaxshiroq!

questions.prompt: Do you enjoy looking at the stars at night?
questions.sampleA1: Yes. I like stars. They are shiny. Night.
questions.sampleA2: Yes, I like stars. They are pretty and I like to see them at night. But I can't see many stars because I live in the city. It's sad.
questions.sampleB1: Yes, I enjoy looking at the stars at night. I think it's very beautiful. However, it's difficult to see many stars where I live because of the lights. For example, when I go to the countryside, I can see more stars and it's amazing.
questions.sampleB2: Absolutely, I find stargazing incredibly relaxing. There's something magical about gazing up at a clear night sky and realising just how small we are. Unfortunately, living in the city, light pollution gets in the way, so I don't see many. But whenever I head out to the countryside, I make the most of it.
questions.uzSampleA1: Ha. Men yulduzlarni yaxshi ko'raman. Ular yorqin. Kechasi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Ha, menga yulduzlar yoqadi. Ular chiroyli va men ularni kechasi ko'rishni yaxshi ko'raman. Lekin men ko'p yulduzlarni ko'ra olmayman, chunki men shaharda yashayman. Bu juda achinarli.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Ha, men kechasi yulduzlarga qarashni yoqtiraman. Menimcha, bu juda go'zal.
Lekin, men yashaydigan joyda chiroqlar tufayli ko'p yulduzlarni ko'rish qiyin.
Masalan, qishloqqa borganimda, men ko'proq yulduzlarni ko'ra olaman va bu ajoyib.
questions.uzSampleB2: Ha, men tunlari yulduzlarga qarashni juda yoqtiraman. Tungi osmonni kuzatishda o'ziga xos xotirjamlik bor, garchi shahardan yorug'lik ifloslanishi tufayli buni qilish ko'pincha qiyin bo'lsa ham. Qishloq joylarga borish imkoniyati tug'ilganda, men yulduzlarni kuzatishga vaqt ajratishga harakat qilaman. Bu tinchlantiruvchi tajriba va koinotning ulkanligini eslatib turadi.

vocabulary.title: Q3 - Do you enjoy looking at the stars at night?
idioms: We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars - "Biz hammamiz chuqurlikdamiz, lekin ba'zilarimiz yulduzlarga qarayapmiz"
reach for the stars - "yulduzlarga intilmoq"
once in a blue moon - "juda kamdan-kam"
phrases: puts things into perspective - "narsalarga boshqacha qarashga majbur qiladi"
sentenceStarters: "Absolutely, I love looking at the stars..." - "Albatta, men yulduzlarga qarashni yaxshi ko'raman..."
"Unfortunately, living in a city means..." - "Afsuski, shaharda yashash ... degani"
"Looking at the stars always makes me think about..." - "Yulduzlarga qarash meni doim ... haqida o'ylashga majbur qiladi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Absolutely, I love looking at the stars at night. There's something truly magical about gazing up at a clear night sky.
Unfortunately, living in a city means I don't get to see many stars due to light pollution. But whenever I visit the countryside or go camping, I make sure to spend some time stargazing. It's an incredibly peaceful and humbling experience.
Looking at the stars always makes me think about how vast the universe is and how small we are in comparison. It puts everyday problems into perspective. As they say, "We are all in the gutter, but some of us are looking at the stars".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Albatta, men kechasi yulduzlarga qarashni yaxshi ko'raman. Tiniq osmonga tikilishda haqiqatan ham sehrli bir narsa bor.

Afsuski, shaharda yashashim tufayli yorug'lik ifloslanishi sababli ko'p yulduzlarni ko'ra olmayman. Ammo qishloqqa borganimda yoki sayohatga chiqqanimda, albatta, yulduzlarga qarashga vaqt ajrataman. Bu juda tinch va kamtarona tajriba.

Yulduzlarga qarash har doim menga koinot naqadar kengligi va biz unga nisbatan naqadar kichik ekanligimiz haqida o'ylashga majbur qiladi. Bu kundalik muammolarni nuqtai nazarga qo'yadi. Aytishlaricha, "Biz hammamiz ariqda yotibmiz, lekin ba'zilarimiz yulduzlarga qarayapmiz".

questions.prompt: What do you see in these pictures?
questions.sampleA2: I see a cinema. There are many people. And I see a sofa. A family is watching TV. It's different.
questions.sampleB1: In the pictures, I can see people watching films. In one picture, they are at the cinema. It looks very crowded. In the other picture, they are at home, on a sofa. I think it is more comfortable at home, but the cinema is more exciting.
questions.sampleB2: Well, these two pictures both show people enjoying their leisure time and eating popcorn, but in very different settings. In the first one, a group of friends or family are at a cinema, clearly having a great time. The young woman in the foreground is smiling broadly and holding a bucket of popcorn, suggesting they're watching something amusing. By contrast, the second picture shows a couple relaxing at home on a sofa. They're also sharing popcorn and looking very happy, perhaps settling down to watch a movie. So, while one depicts a public outing, the other is a private moment, but both capture the joy of shared entertainment.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men kinoteatrni ko'ryapman. U yerda ko'p odamlar bor. Va men divanni ko'ryapman. Bir oila televizor ko'ryapti. Bu boshqacha.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Rasmlarda odamlarni kino ko'rayotganini ko'rishim mumkin. Bir rasmda ular kinoteatrda. U juda gavjumga o'xshaydi.
Boshqa rasmda ular uyda, divanda. Menimcha, uyda qulayroq, lekin kinoteatr qiziqarliroq.
questions.uzSampleB2: Rasmlarda filmlarni tomosha qilishning ikki xil usuli tasvirlangan. Birida an'anaviy kinoteatr muhiti ko'rsatilgan, ko'p odamlar birga yig'ilgan, ehtimol, jamoaviy tajribani baham ko'rishmoqda. Ikkinchisida esa, yanada shaxsiy va samimiy muhit ko'rsatilgan, oila a'zolari o'zlarining yashash xonasida film tomosha qilishmoqda. Kinoteatr jamoatchilik hissi va tomoshani taqdim etadiganga o'xshaydi, uy muhiti esa qulaylik va nazoratni ta'minlaydi. Ikkalasi ham film tomosha qilish tajribasida nimani qidirayotganingizga qarab, o'z afzalliklariga ega.

vocabulary.title: Q4 - What do you see in these pictures?
idioms: a picture is worth a thousand words - "bir rasm ming so'zga arziydi"
there's no place like home - "uydan yaxshi joy yo'q"
the best of both worlds - "ikki dunyoning eng yaxshisi"
sentenceStarters: "These two pictures show different ways of..." - "Bu ikki rasm ... ning turli usullarini ko'rsatadi"
"In the first picture, I can see..." - "Birinchi rasmda men ... ko'ryapman"
"The second picture shows..." - "Ikkinchi rasm ... ko'rsatadi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
These two pictures show different ways of enjoying movies.
In the first picture, I can see a crowded movie theater where people are sitting in the dark, looking up at a large screen. Some of them appear to be eating popcorn, which is a classic part of the cinema experience. The atmosphere looks exciting and immersive.
The second picture shows a couple or family relaxing on a cozy sofa at home, wearing comfortable clothes and watching a movie on their TV. This looks like a much more laid-back and intimate way to enjoy a film, where they can pause, rewind, and feel completely at ease in their own space.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Bu ikki rasm filmlardan zavqlanishning turli usullarini ko'rsatadi.

Birinchi rasmda men odamlar qorong'ida o'tirgan, katta ekranga qarab turgan gavjum kinoteatrni ko'rishim mumkin. Ularning ba'zilari popkorn yeyayotganga o'xshaydi, bu kino tajribasining klassik qismidir. Atmosfera hayajonli va immersiv ko'rinadi.

Ikkinchi rasmda bir juftlik yoki oila uyda qulay divanda dam olayotgani, qulay kiyimlar kiyib, televizorda film tomosha qilayotgani ko'rsatilgan. Bu filmdan zavqlanishning ancha xotirjam va samimiy usuli bo'lib ko'rinadi, ular to'xtatib qo'yishlari, orqaga qaytarishlari va o'z joylarida butunlay bemalol his qilishlari mumkin.

questions.prompt: What are the advantages of watching a film in a traditional cinema?
questions.sampleA1: Cinema is good. Big screen. I like it.
questions.sampleA2: I like the cinema. It's big and loud. I can see the movie with my friends, and we eat popcorn. But it's expensive.
questions.sampleB1: I think going to the cinema is better than watching at home. For example, the screen is much bigger, so it's more exciting. Also, the sound is better. However, it can be expensive, and sometimes people talk during the movie.
questions.sampleB2: Well, the biggest draw for me is definitely the immersive experience. The huge screen and surround sound completely pull you into the film in a way your TV simply can't match. On top of that, it's a great social outing — you get to share the laughs and the scares with a whole room. That said, the tickets don't come cheap.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men kinoteatrni yaxshi ko'raman. U katta va shovqinli. Men filmni do'stlarim bilan ko'rishim mumkin va biz popkorn yeymiz. Lekin u qimmat.
questions.uzSampleB1:
Menimcha, kinoga borish uyda tomosha qilishdan yaxshiroq.
Masalan, ekran ancha katta, shuning uchun u yanada hayajonliroq. Shuningdek, ovoz ham yaxshiroq.
Biroq, bu qimmat bo'lishi mumkin va ba'zida odamlar film davomida gaplashadi.
questions.uzSampleB2: Xo'sh, bir afzalligi, albatta, immersiv tajribadir. Katta ekran va atrof-muhit ovozi sizni haqiqatan ham filmga shunday tortadiki, uyingizdagi televizoringiz bunga tenglasha olmaydi. Qolaversa, bu maxsus joy; sizning telefoningiz yoki uydagi boshqa narsalar sizni chalg'itishi ehtimoli kamroq. Biroq, shuni aytish kerakki, narx ba'zi odamlar uchun to'siq bo'lishi mumkin va shovqinli tomoshabinlar ba'zan tajribani buzishi mumkin.

vocabulary.title: Q5 - What are the advantages of watching a film in a traditional cinema?
idioms: Life is like a movie, write your own ending - "Hayot kino kabi, o'z yakuningizni yozing"
on the edge of your seat - "hayajondan o'tirgani joy topolmaslik"
steal the show - "hammaning e'tiborini tortmoq"
sentenceStarters: "There are several notable advantages to..." - "... ning bir nechta e'tiborga molik afzalliklari bor"
"Firstly, the big screen experience is..." - "Birinchidan, katta ekran tajribasi ..."
"Additionally, the cinema forces you to..." - "Bundan tashqari, kinoteatr sizni ... ga majbur qiladi"

questions.sampleAnswer:
There are several notable advantages to watching a film in a traditional cinema, as depicted in the first picture.
Firstly, the big screen experience is something you simply cannot replicate at home. The massive screen combined with surround sound creates an incredibly immersive atmosphere that draws you completely into the story.
Secondly, going to the cinema is a social activity. It's a wonderful way to spend time with friends or family, and sharing the experience of laughing or being moved by a film with a room full of strangers adds something truly special.
Additionally, the cinema forces you to disconnect from distractions — you put your phone away and give the film your full attention. At home, it's tempting to check messages or pause the movie. As they say, "Life is like a movie, write your own ending".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
An'anaviy kinoteatrda film tomosha qilishning bir qancha sezilarli afzalliklari bor, buni birinchi rasmda ko'rish mumkin.

Birinchidan, katta ekranda tomosha qilish tajribasini uyda takrorlashning iloji yo'q. Ulkan ekran va atrofdagi ovoz birgalikda sizni butunlay hikoyaga tortadigan nihoyatda hayratlanarli muhit yaratadi.

Ikkinchidan, kinoga borish - bu ijtimoiy faoliyat. Bu do'stlar yoki oila bilan vaqt o'tkazishning ajoyib usuli va bir xona to'la notanish odamlar bilan filmdan kulish yoki ta'sirlanish tajribasini baham ko'rish chinakamiga o'zgacha bir narsa qo'shadi.

Bundan tashqari, kinoteatr sizni chalg'ituvchi omillardan uzoqlashishga majbur qiladi - siz telefoningizni o'chirib qo'yasiz va filmga butun e'tiboringizni qaratasiz. Uyda esa xabarlarni tekshirish yoki filmni to'xtatib turish vasvasaga soladi. Aytishlaricha, "Hayot kino kabi, o'z yakuningizni yozing".

questions.prompt: Why do some people prefer to watch movies in the comfort of their own home?
questions.sampleA1: I like movies. I like home. Home is good.
questions.sampleA2: I like watch movies at home. It is good because I can relax. And I can eat pizza. The cinema is expensive, but home is cheap.
questions.sampleB1: Some people like to watch movies at home because it's more comfortable. I think it's true. At home, you can wear pajamas and sit on your sofa. Also, it's cheaper than going to the cinema. For example, you don't have to buy expensive popcorn. However, the cinema has a bigger screen.
questions.sampleB2: I suppose the main reason is the sheer comfort of it. At home you can curl up on the sofa in your pyjamas, pause whenever you like, and snack without paying over the odds. On top of that, streaming services put thousands of films at your fingertips for a small monthly fee. For a lot of people, that convenience simply wins out.
questions.uzSampleA1: Men kinolarni yaxshi ko'raman. Men uyni yaxshi ko'raman. Uy yaxshi.
questions.uzSampleA2: Men uyda kino ko'rishni yaxshi ko'raman. Bu yaxshi, chunki men dam olishim mumkin. Va men pizza yeyishim mumkin. Kinoteatr qimmat, lekin uy arzon.
questions.uzSampleB1: Ba'zi odamlar filmlarni uyda ko'rishni yaxshi ko'radilar, chunki bu qulayroq. Menimcha, bu to'g'ri. Uyda siz pijamada yurishingiz va divaningizda o'tirishingiz mumkin. Bundan tashqari, bu kinoga borishdan arzonroq. Masalan, siz qimmatbaho popkorn sotib olishingiz shart emas. Biroq, kinoteatrda ekran kattaroq bo'ladi.
questions.uzSampleB2:
Ko'pchilik odamlar filmlarni o'z uyida tomosha qilishni afzal ko'rishadi va buning bir nechta sabablari bor.
Birinchidan, qulaylik omili asosiy sabablardan biridir. Siz atrof-muhitni to'liq nazorat qilasiz – filmni to'xtatib qo'yishingiz, ovoz balandligini sozlashingiz va umuman olganda tajribani o'zingizga moslashtirishingiz mumkin.
Ikkinchidan, narx ko'pincha muhim omil hisoblanadi. Oylik to'lov evaziga filmlarning katta kutubxonasini taklif qiluvchi striming xizmatlari bilan kinoteatrga tez-tez borishdan ko'ra bu ko'pincha tejamkorroqdir.
Va nihoyat, ba'zi odamlar kinoteatrning muhitini chalg'ituvchi deb bilishadi, o'z uyining shaxsiy hayoti va yaqinligini afzal ko'rishadi.

vocabulary.title: Q6 - Why do some people prefer to watch movies in the comfort of their own home?
idioms: Home is where the heart is - "Uy - yurak turgan joy"
make yourself at home - "o'zingizni uyingizdek his qiling"
couch potato - "divandan turmaydigan odam"
sentenceStarters: "Many people increasingly prefer watching movies at home..." - "Ko'pchilik tobora ko'proq uyda kino ko'rishni afzal ko'rmoqda..."
"Primarily, the comfort factor is..." - "Birinchi navbatda, qulaylik omili ..."
"Moreover, it's significantly cheaper than..." - "Bundan tashqari, bu ... ga nisbatan ancha arzon"

questions.sampleAnswer:
Many people increasingly prefer watching movies at home, as shown in the second picture, and there are several convincing reasons for this.
Primarily, the comfort factor is unbeatable. At home, you can wear whatever you like, lie on your sofa with a blanket, and eat your own snacks without paying ridiculously high cinema prices. It's a much more relaxed experience.
Furthermore, streaming services like Netflix and Amazon Prime have made it incredibly easy to access thousands of films from your living room. You have the freedom to choose what to watch, when to watch it, and you can pause or rewind at any time.
Moreover, it's significantly cheaper than going to the cinema. A family trip to the movies can cost a fortune when you add up tickets, popcorn, and drinks. At home, you can enjoy a movie night for a fraction of the cost. As they say, "Home is where the heart is".
questions.uzSampleAnswer:

Rather than shifting the blame during an argument, a responsible person will hold their hands up, apologise, and work towards a solution. Over time, that honesty builds a solid foundation of mutual understanding that keeps relationships healthy. On top of that, I'd say personal responsibility is the cornerstone of personal growth. It pushes you to take a long, hard look at yourself — your strengths, your weaknesses, and the mistakes you'd rather forget. By owning those lessons instead of brushing them under the carpet, you gradually develop discipline, resilience, and a genuine growth mindset. As the saying goes, the price of greatness is responsibility. At the end of the day, real progress only kicks in once you accept that your life is shaped, first and foremost, by your own choices — and nobody else's.

bulletPoints: How does taking personal responsibility influence a person's success?
What role does personal responsibility play in building strong relationships?
How can practicing personal responsibility lead to personal growth?
questions.sampleAnswer:
Personal responsibility and success:
Taking personal responsibility is fundamentally important for achieving success in life. When you take ownership of your actions, you stop blaming external factors and start focusing on what you can control. This mindset naturally leads to better decision-making, stronger work ethic, and a proactive approach to overcoming challenges.
Personal responsibility in relationships:
In relationships, personal responsibility plays a crucial role. When people take responsibility for their words and actions, it builds trust and respect. Instead of pointing fingers during conflicts, responsible individuals acknowledge their mistakes and work towards solutions. This creates a foundation of mutual understanding that strengthens bonds over time.
Personal responsibility and personal growth:
Practicing personal responsibility is essentially the cornerstone of personal growth. It encourages self-reflection — you learn to evaluate your strengths and weaknesses honestly. By holding yourself accountable, you develop discipline, resilience, and a growth mindset. As they say, "The price of greatness is responsibility". True growth begins when you accept that your life is shaped by your own choices.
questions.uzSampleAnswer:
Shaxsiy mas'uliyat va muvaffaqiyat:
Shaxsiy mas'uliyatni o'z zimmasiga olish hayotda muvaffaqiyatga erishish uchun juda muhimdir. O'z harakatlaringizga egalik qilsangiz, tashqi omillarni ayblashni to'xtatasiz va o'zingiz nazorat qila oladigan narsalarga e'tibor qaratasiz. Bu fikrlash tarzi, tabiiyki, yaxshiroq qarorlar qabul qilishga, kuchli mehnat axloqiga va qiyinchiliklarni yengish uchun faol yondashuvga olib keladi.
Munosabatlarda shaxsiy mas'uliyat:
Munosabatlarda shaxsiy mas'uliyat muhim rol o'ynaydi. Odamlar o'z so'zlari va harakatlari uchun javobgarlikni o'z zimmalariga olganda, bu ishonch va hurmatni shakllantiradi. Mojarolar paytida ayblash o'rniga, mas'uliyatli shaxslar o'z xatolarini tan oladilar va yechimlar ustida ishlaydilar. Bu vaqt o'tishi bilan aloqalarni mustahkamlaydigan o'zaro tushunish asosini yaratadi.
Shaxsiy mas'uliyat va shaxsiy o'sish:
Shaxsiy mas'uliyatni amalda qo'llash, asosan, shaxsiy o'sishning asosidir. Bu o'z-o'zini tahlil qilishni rag'batlantiradi — siz o'z kuchli va zaif tomonlaringizni halol baholashni o'rganasiz. O'zingizni javobgar qilib, intizom, chidamlilik va o'sish fikrlash tarzini rivojlantirasiz. Aytishlaricha, "Buyuklikning narxi - mas'uliyat". Haqiqiy o'sish hayotingiz o'z tanlovingiz bilan shakllanganini qabul qilganingizda boshlanadi.

questions.prompt: All countries should adapt to a 4-day work week.
questions.sampleA1: Work four days? Yes, I like. More free time. Good.
questions.sampleA2: I think four days is good. I like to work less and have more time for fun. But maybe the work is not finished so it is bad.
questions.sampleB1: I think a four-day work week is a good idea. In my opinion, people would be happier and less stressed. For example, they could spend more time with their families. However, I think it might be difficult for some companies to do this, especially if they need to be open every day.
questions.sampleB2: This is a really hot topic these days, and to be honest, I can see strong arguments on both sides of the fence. On the one hand, the supporters of a four-day week make a pretty compelling case. The obvious benefit is a much healthier work-life balance — with an extra day off, people have more time to recharge their batteries, spend time with family, and pursue their hobbies. Believe it or not, several trials have shown that productivity actually goes up rather than down, because well-rested employees tend to knuckle down and work far more efficiently. On top of that, a shorter week can help to prevent burnout, which is a growing problem in so many industries nowadays. On the other hand, the critics do raise some valid concerns. For a start, it's not a one-size-fits-all solution — certain sectors, like healthcare or hospitality, simply can't afford to shut up shop for an extra day. Rolling out such a big change would also call for a major overhaul of how businesses operate, and smaller companies might struggle to make ends meet. There's a real risk that customer service could suffer if firms aren't staffed properly. All things considered, though, I'm broadly in favour of the idea. I genuinely believe that if it's rolled out gradually and tailored to each industry, with proper support for the sectors that need it most, the benefits would outweigh the drawbacks in the long run. After all, working smarter rather than harder is surely the way forward.

Bundan tashqari, u kompaniyalarga ko'proq iste'dodlarni jalb qilishi mumkin. Biroq, bunday o'zgarishni amalga oshirish diqqat bilan rejalashtirish va ko'rib chiqishni talab qiladi. questions.sampleAnswer:
This is a highly relevant topic in today's working world, with strong arguments on both sides.
Supporters of the 4-day work week argue that it significantly improves work-life balance. With an extra day off, employees have more time for family, hobbies, and rest, which leads to happier and more motivated workers. Moreover, studies have shown that shorter work weeks can actually boost productivity, as employees tend to be more focused and efficient when they have less time. Additionally, reduced working days help lower stress and prevent burnout, which is a growing problem in many professions.
However, critics raise valid concerns. In certain industries, such as healthcare, emergency services, and manufacturing, reducing work days could seriously impact productivity and service delivery. Businesses would need major restructuring — adjusting schedules, hiring additional staff, and reorganising workflows, which could be costly. Furthermore, some essential services might suffer from limited availability, potentially inconveniencing the public.
Personally, I believe a 4-day work week could work well in many sectors, but it shouldn't be a one-size-fits-all policy. Each industry should evaluate what works best. As they say, "All work and no play makes Jack a dull boy".
